build.prompt: One continuous, unbroken cinematic camera move of a kitchen being installed, like a satisfying timelapse. The camera starts high near the ceiling, looking steeply down at the panels, the terrazzo slab and the boxes laid out on the oak floor like a floor plan, then glides smoothly down and back, tilting up to eye level until it faces the back wall straight on. As the camera moves: the flat oak panels lift off their stacks one by one and fly to the back wall, where they slot together at right angles into box-shaped cabinet carcasses for the tall units and the wall cabinets; the oak doors swing shut onto them one after another on their hinges; where the stacks lay, the butter-yellow lacquered panels lift and slot together at right angles into a row of rigid box cabinets that becomes the long island; the terrazzo slab rises from its trestles in one solid piece and lowers onto the island; the tap rises into place, the two white pendants lower from the ceiling and the oak stools slide in. Every panel is a rigid, flat board 18 mm thick that never bends, folds, curls or flexes: panels only move, turn and click together edge to edge, like real cabinetry being assembled. Precise, calm, satisfying motion. The room itself stays exactly the same throughout: the white plaster walls, the ceiling, the oak floor, the window, the curtain and the bright morning sun.
